title: Just started to develop a game in Godot with Codex
author: gaxelbrodie
selftext:
It would be a fully procedural (no assets at all) 2D dungeon exploration rogue-like and I'm using Codex in VS Code to build it using GDScript as a language.

I've ChatGPT Plus that's enough for now. My workflow is basically to come up with ideas, fixes, gameplay changes, etc, brainstorm it with ChatGPT on browser, and when I'm sure I'm in the right direction, ask to create a prompt, read and fix it and then use it in a (new) chat in VS Code Codex. I'm usually using a new chat to minimize tokens usage, since I've added to the project an [AGENTS.md](http://AGENTS.md) file with all the specifications I wanted for this project that also tell the AI to first read a PROJECT\_STATUS.md and update it after it has finished with the prompt. In this way any new chat should know what to do and where. Also every new chat is tied to a specific feature, where I use Sol medium, high or very high based on the task, in this way I can make "small" changes every time and test it before committing them, and also returning to older chat to make specific changes keeping everything separated.

I'm a web developer and I worked on Unity or XNA before, in my spare time, so I know how a game works, sadly I've been always held back and scared by the time required to just see something moving on screen, so I decided  (just like I'm doing at work) to use AI to write everything and just be the director and designer. 

What I'd like to know is if this is a good way to "vibe code" at least a prototype that could then become a early access game, or if it could be done in a better way. Also, this would be a fully AI project, so I don't know if that should be mentioned in case of publishing something, or if it's even mandatory on Steam, for example.

comments.author: Early_Flamingo5337
comments.body: My honest opinion is to first think about if your idea, mechanics and gameplay brings something really new and worth playing over other games as your genre is pretty much crowded, unless you are just doing it for yourself, for fun. Then you could actually just explore with no issues.

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
I wouldn't do that. I ruined so many good ideas because I didn't start with the right ruleset and didn't want to fix the mess afterwards. 


Sure in general you would start with a game play idea or vision. But then I would put a couple hundred thousand tokens into a good ruleset for the agents. Especially if you plan on multitasking with multiple agents

replies.author: Early_Flamingo5337
replies.body: But what's the point of spending tons of tokens in a gameplay if it is at the end very similar to other hundreds of games out there? As I said, unless you want something for yourself

comments.author: newgenesisscion
comments.body:
Use a Godot MCP, it really helps with making the game. You can connect it to Codex.

I'd also recommend using ChatGPT's imagegen skill to create mock ups and concepts.

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body:
One critical thing I learned. 
Keep the file size under 300 lines of code per file + a header what the code does. Huge help when ai finds things very fast in a big codebase
